papers.title: Unfinished-Bench: Measuring Rule Violations by Persistent Agents in Realistic Work Environments
papers.problem: AI agents that keep working alone break hidden workplace rules, and nobody measured how often.
papers.fix: Persistence raised rule breaking from 32.2% to 43.6% for rules in documents, versus 8.5% for rules the user stated.
papers.practicalUseCase: A rule buried in a file is much weaker than a rule you say; state key limits in the prompt.
papers.limitation: The test used 97 made-up work scenarios, so real workplaces may differ.

papers.title: How Far Can Untrained Neural Networks Go in Anomaly Detection? From Tables to Pixels
papers.problem: Anomaly detection usually needs trained features, so nobody knew how well a model with no training does.
papers.fix: Fixed random features plus a simple distance score reached 86.4% mean AUROC on 47 tabular datasets, with no training.
papers.practicalUseCase: Try this cheap untrained baseline first; train a model only if it clearly beats it.
papers.limitation: It was tested on benchmark datasets only, not live production data.

papers.title: General progress substitutes for specific training data in language models
papers.problem: Developers withhold data to block risky skills in language models, but nobody knew how long that delay lasts.
papers.fix: General progress on other data replaces withheld data, so models relearn the skill from a small fraction of the data.
papers.practicalUseCase: Data filtering only delays a risky skill, so do not rely on it alone for safety.
papers.limitation: Tests used chess, Othello, molecular strings, bracket languages, web text, and one programming language on a 7-billion-parameter model.

papers.title: Replay, Don't Resample: Off-Policy Consolidation of Long-Horizon RL Experts
papers.problem: Merging many expert models into one is costly, because the student must sample every environment again.
papers.fix: Replaying expert training logs in order beat the standard merge method, using about one seventh of training compute.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you train several experts, keep their logs and replay them in order instead of resampling.
papers.limitation: It was tested on three domains only: reasoning, search, and SQL.

papers.title: Islamic Social Financial Instruments and Sustainable Community Development: Evidence Synthesis on Community Resilience
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Research on zakat, waqf, and sadaqah is scattered, so it is unclear how they help communities cope with shocks.
papers.fix: Across 93 studies, zakat gives short-term relief, waqf builds long-term assets, and sadaqah gives flexible emergency help.
papers.practicalUseCase: Combined zakat, waqf, and sadaqah models work best, so plan giving programs as one system with strong governance.
papers.limitation: It reviews past studies, so its conclusions are only as strong as those studies.

papers.title: Trends and Determinants of Sustainability Sukuk Issuance: Evidence from Global Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Sustainability sukuk are growing fast, but nobody had documented how they are issued or what drives issue size.
papers.fix: Across 11,944 sukuk issued from 2012 to 2022, equity-based contracts, social purposes, and government issuers produced larger issues.
papers.practicalUseCase: Costly second party opinions shrink issue size, so cutting that cost could help more issuers join.
papers.limitation: The data covers 2012 to 2022 only and shows links, not cause.

papers.title: From Clicks to Credit: AI-Measured Halal Product Awareness and Halal Financing Depth across OIC Countries
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Nobody knew whether consumer interest in halal products moves the amount of Islamic financing banks provide.
papers.fix: Online halal search interest significantly raised total Islamic financing in 16 OIC countries, mainly through Murabaha and Ijarah contracts.
papers.practicalUseCase: Banks can read search trends to forecast demand, mostly for simple Murabaha and Ijarah products.
papers.limitation: It covers 16 countries from 2014 to 2023, and search volume only proxies awareness.

papers.title: Islamic Banking Products Accessibility and SME Performance: Evaluating Shari’ah-Compliant Financial Solutions for Somali Enterprises
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.leadAuthor: Ali Yassin Sheikh Ali et al.
papers.problem: Somali small businesses lack clear evidence on which parts of Shari'ah-compliant banking actually improve their performance.
papers.fix: Affordability and ease of access drove business performance most, while awareness alone had little direct effect.
papers.practicalUseCase: Cheaper and easier Islamic banking helps small firms more than awareness campaigns, so banks should fix cost and process first.
papers.limitation: It surveyed business owners in one city, Baidoa, at one point in time.

papers.title: Examining the Impact of Waqf Literacy on Waqf Behaviour
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Waqf collections stay low, and it was unclear whether better waqf knowledge changes what Muslims actually give.
papers.fix: Among 642 Indonesian respondents, waqf literacy raised attitude, social norms, and control, which indirectly raised waqf intention.
papers.practicalUseCase: Teaching people about waqf can raise giving, so waqf bodies should invest in education.
papers.limitation: It measures intention from a survey in Indonesia, not actual donations.
